plan: 1 Kings 13:1-34; 1 Kings 14:1-18, 21-24; 2 Chronicles 12:13-14; 2 Chronicles 11:18-23; 2 Chronicles 12:1-12; 1 Kings 14:25-28; 2 Chronicles 12:15-16; 1 Kings 14:29-31; 1 Kings 15:1-5; 2 Chronicles 13:1–14:1; 1 Kings 15:6-8; 2 Chronicles 14:2-8; 1 Kings 15:9-15; 1 Kings 14:19-20; 1 Kings 15:25-26, 27-34; 2 Chronicles 14:9-15; 2 Chronicles 15:1-19

readings.title: The Man of Elohim and the Lying Prophet
readings.subtitle: A Prophecy Against Jeroboam's Altar and the Consequence of Disobedience
readings.text:
[1 Kings 13:1] And see, a man of <dn>Elohim</dn> went from Yehuḏah to Běyth Ěl by the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, while Yaroḇ‛am was standing by the slaughter-place to burn incense.
[2] And he cried out against the slaughter-place by the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and said, “O slaughter-place, slaughter-place! Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>‘See, a son is to be born to the house of Daviḏ, Yoshiyahu is his name. And on you he shall slaughter <dn>את</dn> the priests of the high places who burn incense on you, and men’s bones be burned on you.’</dq> ”
[3] And he gave a sign the same day, saying, “This is the sign which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has spoken: <dq>See, the slaughter-place is split apart, and the ashes on it is poured out.</dq>”
[4] And it came to be when Sovereign Yaroḇ‛am heard the saying of the man of <dn>Elohim</dn>, who cried out against the slaughter-place in Běyth Ěl, that he stretched out his hand from the slaughter-place, saying, “Seize him!” Then his hand, which he stretched out toward him, dried up, so that he was unable to bring it back to him.
[5] And the slaughter-place was split apart, and the ashes poured out from the slaughter-place, according to the sign which the man of <dn>Elohim</dn> had given by the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.
[6] And the sovereign answered and said to the man of <dn>Elohim</dn>, “Please appease <dn>את</dn> the face of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, and pray for me, that my hand might be restored to me.” And the man of <dn>Elohim</dn> appeased <dn>את</dn> the face of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and the sovereign’s hand was restored to him, and became as it was before.
[7] The sovereign then said to the man of <dn>Elohim</dn>, “Come home with me and refresh yourself, and I give you a gift.”
[8] But the man of <dn>Elohim</dn> said to the sovereign, “If you were to give me half your house, I do not go in with you, nor do I eat bread nor drink water in this place.
[9] “For so <dn>He</dn> commanded me by the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, saying, <dq>‘Do not eat bread, nor drink water, nor return by the same way you came.’</dq> ”
[10] So he went another way and did not return by the way he came to Běyth Ěl.
[11] And a certain old prophet was dwelling in Běyth Ěl, and his sons came and told him all the works that the man of <dn>Elohim</dn> had done that day in Běyth Ěl, the words which he had spoken to the sovereign.
[12] And their father said to them, “Which way did he go?” And his sons had seen which way the man of <dn>Elohim</dn> went who came from Yehuḏah.
[13] And he said to his sons, “Saddle the donkey for me.” And they saddled the donkey for him, and he rode on it,
[14] and went after the man of <dn>Elohim</dn>, and found him sitting under a terebinth. And he said to him, “Are you the man of <dn>Elohim</dn> who came from Yehuḏah?” And he said, “<dn>I</dn> am.”
[15] And he said to him, “Come home with me and eat bread.”
[16] And he said, “I am not able to return with you or to go in with you, nor am I to eat bread or drink water with you in this place.
[17] “For word came to me by the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>‘Do not eat bread nor drink water there, nor return by going the way you came.’</dq> ”
[18] And he said to him, “I too am a prophet like you, and a messenger spoke to me by the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, saying, <dq>‘Bring him back with you to your house, and let him eat bread and drink water.’</dq> ” But he lied to him.
[19] So he turned back with him, and ate bread in his house, and drank water.
[20] And it came to be, as they sat at the table, that the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came to the prophet who had brought him back,
[21] and he cried out to the man of <dn>Elohim</dn> who came from Yehuḏah, saying, “Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>‘Because you have rebelled against the mouth of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and have not guarded <dn>את</dn> the command which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> commanded you,</dq>
[22] <dq>and turned back, and ate bread, and drank water in the place of which <dn>He</dn> said to you, “Do not eat bread nor drink water,” your body shall not enter the burial-site of your fathers.’</dq> ”
[23] And it came to be, after he had eaten bread and after he had drunk, that he saddled the donkey for him, for the prophet whom he had brought back.
[24] And he went, and a lion met him on the way and killed him. And his body was thrown on the way. And the donkey was standing by it, and the lion was standing by the body.
[25] And see, men were passing by and saw the body thrown on the way, while the lion was standing by the body. And they went and reported it in the city where the old prophet dwelt.
[26] And the prophet who had brought him back from the way heard it, and said, “It is the man of <dn>Elohim</dn> who rebelled against the mouth of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> gave him to the lion, and it tore him apart and killed him, according to the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> which <dn>He</dn> spoke to him.”
[27] And he spoke to his sons, saying, “Saddle the donkey for me.” And they saddled it.
[28] So he went and found his body thrown on the way, and the donkey and the lion standing by the body. The lion had not eaten <dn>את</dn> the body nor mauled <dn>את</dn> the donkey.
[29] And the prophet lifted up the body of the man of <dn>Elohim</dn>, and placed it on the donkey, and brought it back. And the old prophet came to the city to mourn, and to bury him,
[30] and he placed his body in his own burial-site. And they lamented over him, saying, “Oh, my brother!”
[31] And it came to be, after he had buried him, that he spoke to his sons, saying, “When I am dead, then you shall bury me in the burial-site where the man of <dn>Elohim</dn> is buried. Lay my bones beside his bones.
[32] “For the word which he cried out, by the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, against the slaughter-place in Běyth Ěl, and against all the houses of the high places which are in the cities of Shomeron, shall certainly come to be.”
[33] After this event Yaroḇ‛am did not turn from his evil way, but again he made priests from all sorts of people for the high places. Whoever wished, he ordained, to become one of the priests of the high places.
[34] And this matter was the sin of the house of Yaroḇ‛am, even to cut it off and destroy <dn>את</dn> it from the face of the earth.

readings.subsection: The Reigns of Jeroboam and Rehoboam
readings.title: Prophecy Against Jeroboam's House
readings.subtitle: The Sickness of Abijah and the Idolatry of Judah
readings.text:
[1 Kings 14:1] At that time Aḇiyah the son of Yaroḇ‛am became sick.
[2] And Yaroḇ‛am said to his wife, “Please arise, and disguise yourself, so they do not know that you are the wife of Yaroḇ‛am, and go to Shiloh. See, Aḥiyah the prophet is there, who spoke to me of becoming sovereign over this people.
[3] “And you shall take with you ten loaves, and cakes, and a jar of honey, and go to him. Let him declare to you what becomes of the child.”
[4] And Yaroḇ‛am’s wife did so, and rose up and went to Shiloh, and came to the house of Aḥiyah. But Aḥiyahu was unable to see, for his eyes had set because of his age.
[5] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had said to Aḥiyahu, <dq>“See, the wife of Yaroḇ‛am is coming to ask you a word about her son, for he is sick. Speak to her thus and thus. For it shall be, when she comes in, that she makes herself strange.”</dq>
[6] And it came to be, when Aḥiyahu heard the sound of her footsteps as she came through the door, he said, “Come in, wife of Yaroḇ‛am. Why are you making yourself strange? And <dn>I</dn> have been sent to you with a hard word.
[7] Go, say to Yaroḇ‛am, <dq>‘Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl, “Because <dn>I</dn> exalted you from among the people, and made you ruler over <dn>My</dn> people Yisra’ěl,</dq>
[8] <dq>and tore <dn>את</dn> the reign away from the house of Daviḏ, and gave it to you – and you have not been as <dn>My</dn> servant Daviḏ, who guarded <dn>My</dn> commands and who followed <dn>Me</dn> with all his heart, to do only what was right in <dn>My</dn> eyes,</dq>
[9] <dq>but you have done more evil than all who were before you, for you have gone and made for yourself other mighty ones and moulded images to provoke <dn>Me</dn>, and have cast <dn>Me</dn> behind your back –</dq>
[10] <dq>therefore, see, <dn>I</dn> am bringing evil to the house of Yaroḇ‛am, and shall cut off from Yaroḇ‛am every male in Yisra’ěl, whether shut up or left at large, and sweep away <dn>את</dn> the remnant of the house of Yaroḇ‛am, as one sweeps away dung until it is all gone.</dq>
[11] <dq>Those of Yaroḇ‛am who die in the city the dogs do eat, and those who die in the field the birds of the heavens do eat, for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has spoken it!” ’</dq>
[12] <dq>“And you, arise, go to your house. When your feet enter the city, the child shall die.</dq>
[13] <dq>“And all Yisra’ěl shall mourn for him and bury him, for he is the only one of Yaroḇ‛am who shall come to the burial-site, because in him there is found a good report toward <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl, in the house of Yaroḇ‛am.</dq>
[14] <dq>“And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall raise up for <dn>Himself</dn> a sovereign over Yisra’ěl who cuts off <dn>את</dn> the house of Yaroḇ‛am, this day, and even now!</dq>
[15] <dq>“And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall strike <dn>את</dn> Yisra’ěl, as a reed is shaken in the water, and shall pluck <dn>את</dn> Yisra’ěl from this good soil which <dn>He</dn> gave to their fathers, and shall scatter them beyond the River, because they made their Ashěrim, provoking <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>,</dq>
[16] <dq>and <dn>He</dn> shall give <dn>את</dn> Yisra’ěl up, because of the sins of Yaroḇ‛am, who sinned and who made Yisra’ěl sin.”</dq>
[17] And the wife of Yaroḇ‛am rose up and went, and came to Tirtsah. When she came to the threshold of the house, the child died.
[18] And they buried him, and all Yisra’ěl lamented for him, according to the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> which <dn>He</dn> spoke through <dn>His</dn> servant Aḥiyahu the prophet.
[21] Meanwhile Reḥaḇ‛am son of Shelomoh reigned in Yehuḏah. Reḥaḇ‛am was forty-one years old when he became sovereign, and he reigned seventeen years in Yerushalayim, the city which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had chosen out of all the tribes of Yisra’ěl, to put <dn>His</dn> Name there. And his mother’s name was Na‛amah the Ammonitess.
[22] And Yehuḏah did evil in the eyes of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and they provoked <dn>Him</dn> to jealousy with their sins which they committed, more than all that their fathers had done.
[23] For they also built for themselves high places, and pillars, and Ashěrim on every high hill and under every green tree.
[24] And there were also cult prostitutes in the land. They did according to all the abominations of the nations which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> dispossessed before the children of Yisra’ěl.

readings.title: Shishak Plunders Jerusalem
readings.subtitle: Rehoboam Replaces Gold Shields with Bronze
readings.text:
[1 Kings 14:25] And it came to be, in the fifth year of Sovereign Reḥaḇ‛am, that Shishaq sovereign of Mitsrayim came up against Yerushalayim.
[26] And he took away <dn>את</dn> the treasures of the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and <dn>את</dn> the treasures of the sovereign’s house, he even took away all. And he took away <dn>את</dn> all the shields of gold which Shelomoh had made.
[27] And Sovereign Reḥaḇ‛am made shields of bronze to replace them, and entrusted them into the hands of the chiefs of the guard, who guarded the entrance of the sovereign’s house.
[28] And it came to be, whenever the sovereign went into the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, the guards would bring them, then take them back into the guardroom.

readings.title: The Death of Rehoboam
readings.subtitle: Abijam Succeeds as King of Judah
readings.text:
[1 Kings 14:29] And the rest of the acts of Reḥaḇ‛am, and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the annals of the sovereigns of Yehuḏah?
[30] And there was fighting between Reḥaḇ‛am and Yaroḇ‛am all the days.
[31] So Reḥaḇ‛am slept with his fathers, and was buried with his fathers in the City of Daviḏ. And the name of his mother was Na‛amah the Ammonitess. And Aḇiyam his son reigned in his place.

readings.title: Abijam Reigns in Judah
readings.subtitle: He Walks in the Sins of His Father
readings.text:
[1 Kings 15:1] And in the eighteenth year of Sovereign Yaroḇ‛am son of Neḇat, Aḇiyam became sovereign over Yehuḏah.
[2] He reigned three years in Yerushalayim, and his mother’s name was Ma‛aḵah the granddaughter of Aḇishalom.
[3] And he walked in all the sins of his father, which he had done before him, and his heart was not perfect to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> his <dn>Elohim</dn>, as was the heart of his father Daviḏ.
[4] But for Daviḏ’s sake <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> his <dn>Elohim</dn> gave him a lamp in Yerushalayim, to raise up his son after him and by establishing Yerushalayim,
[5] for Daviḏ did what was right in the eyes of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and did not turn aside from all that <dn>He</dn> commanded him all the days of his life, except in the matter of Uriyah the Ḥittite.

readings.title: The Death of Abijam
readings.subtitle: Asa Succeeds as King of Judah
readings.text:
[1 Kings 15:6] And there was fighting between Reḥaḇ‛am and Yaroḇ‛am all the days of his life.
[7] And the rest of the acts of Aḇiyam, and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the annals of the sovereigns of Yehuḏah? And there was fighting between Aḇiyam and Yaroḇ‛am.
[8] So Aḇiyam slept with his fathers, and they buried him in the City of Daviḏ. And Asa his son reigned in his place.

readings.title: Asa Reigns in Judah
readings.subtitle: He Does What is Right in the Eyes of YeHoVaH
readings.text:
[1 Kings 15:9] And in the twentieth year of Yaroḇ‛am sovereign of Yisra’ěl, Asa became sovereign over Yehuḏah.
[10] And he reigned forty-one years in Yerushalayim, and his grandmother’s name was Ma‛aḵah the granddaughter of Aḇishalom.
[11] And Asa did what was right in the eyes of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, as his father Daviḏ had done,
[12] and put away the cult prostitutes from the land, and removed <dn>את</dn> all the idols that his fathers had made.
[13] And he also removed <dn>את</dn> Ma‛aḵah his grandmother from being sovereigness mother, because she had made an abominable image for Ashěrah. And Asa cut down <dn>את</dn> her abominable image and burned it by the wadi Qiḏron.
[14] But the high places were not removed. However, Asa’s heart was perfect with <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> all his days.
[15] And he brought into the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>את</dn> the set-apart items of his father, and <dn>את</dn> his own set-apart items: silver and gold and utensils.

readings.title: The Death of Jeroboam
readings.subtitle: Nadab Succeeds as King of Israel
readings.text:
[1 Kings 14:19] And the rest of the acts of Yaroḇ‛am, how he fought and how he reigned, see, they are written in the book of the annals of the sovereigns of Yisra’ěl.
[20] And the days that Yaroḇ‛am reigned was twenty-two years. So he slept with his fathers, and Naḏaḇ his son reigned in his place.

readings.subsection: The Reigns of Nadab and Baasha
readings.title: The Reign and Fall of Nadab
readings.subtitle: Baasha Conspires and Destroys the House of Jeroboam
readings.text:
[1 Kings 15:25] And Naḏaḇ son of Yaroḇ‛am became sovereign over Yisra’ěl in the second year of Asa sovereign of Yehuḏah, and he reigned over Yisra’ěl two years.
[26] And he did evil in the eyes of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and walked in the way of his father, and in his sin by which he had made Yisra’ěl sin.
[27] Then Ba‛asha son of Aḥiyah, of the house of Yissasḵar, conspired against him. And Ba‛asha struck him at Gibbethon, which belonged to the Philistines, for Naḏaḇ and all Yisra’ěl had laid siege to Gibbethon.
[28] And Ba‛asha killed him in the third year of Asa sovereign of Yehuḏah, and reigned in his place.
[29] And it came to be, when he became sovereign, that he struck <dn>את</dn> all the house of Yaroḇ‛am. He did not leave to Yaroḇ‛am anyone breathing, until he had destroyed him, according to the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> which <dn>He</dn> had spoken by <dn>His</dn> servant Aḥiyah the Shilonite,
[30] because of the sins of Yaroḇ‛am, which he had sinned and by which he had made Yisra’ěl sin, because of his provocation with which he had provoked <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl.
[31] And the rest of the acts of Naḏaḇ, and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the annals of the sovereigns of Yisra’ěl?
[32] And there was fighting between Asa and Ba‛asha sovereign of Yisra’ěl all their days.
[33] In the third year of Asa sovereign of Yehuḏah, Ba‛asha son of Aḥiyah became sovereign over all Yisra’ěl in Tirtsah, and reigned twenty-four years.
[34] And he did evil in the eyes of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and walked in the way of Yaroḇ‛am, and in his sin by which he had made Yisra’ěl sin.
